existing_issues.issue: Not wrong, but incomplete/vague. (1) notes 'Advanced classical études; high positions' misses the point: the set is mainly bowing-oriented (varied slurred/detached bowings, spiccato, chords) plus double stops, trills, extensions and shifts up to 9th position; suggest 'Bowing-led études: varied bowings, double stops, trills, shifts' (<=100 chars). (2) exams omits RCM Level 10, where the 2021 syllabus lists 'Gaviniès 24 études (Matinées) PET; INT: any one'; 'AMEB CertPerf (mvt)' and 'ASTA CAP 10' could not be verified here (ameb.edu.au refused automated access; the ASTACAP handbook is members-only). (3) set is empty: use set '24 Matinées' so the 24 new per-study rows group with it. (4) Level 8 is fine for the whole book (individual studies range 6-8). Retailers (e.g. Shar) claim the set covers all 24 keys; the scores use only 16 keys.

new_authors_found: Winn, Edith Lynwood — Boston teacher; Carl Fischer 'How to Study' commentary series (Kreutzer, Fiorillo, Rode, Gaviniès 1923) plus Daily Exercises for Violinists and a revised Halir scale book; check whether the Kreutzer/Fiorillo/Rode researchers list her books
Casorti, August — Technic of the Bow, Op. 50 (cited by Winn as the standard bowing-technique book, Carl Fischer)
Sitt, Hans — Violin Studies Op. 32, Books I-V (position and double-stop studies, cited by Winn)
Halir, Carl — New Scale Studies (double-stop scales; cited by Winn, revised edition by E. L. Winn)
Hřímalý, Jan — Scale Studies (cited by Winn alongside Schradieck and Halir)
Eberhardt, Goby — My System of Practicing the Violin, with Parts I-IV of exercises incl. double stops and bow technique (cited by Winn)
note: WHAT I DID. Numbers, keys, tempo words and metres were read directly from two scans: (a) the Imbault original (Paris, plate 440; BnF Gallica scan, 52 images on Wikimedia Commons, category 'Les Vingt quatre matinées de P. Gaviniès, exercices pour la violon - btv1b9079956h'; study N is image 2N+2 of 52, i.e. No. 1 = 4 of 52 and No. 24 = 50 of 52; printed page 2N) and (b) Peters ed. F. Hermann, EP 1381 (University of Michigan scan on archive.org, item 4724369.0001.001.umich.edu; study N is at archive.org page index n(2N+1), i.e. No. 1 = n3 and No. 24 = n49; printed page 2N). They agree on every number and key signature; tempo words agree apart from the differences listed under TEMPO; metres agree except No. 19 (Imbault shows alla breve, Peters plain C). Independent text confirmation: Wikipedia 'Music written in all major or minor keys' lists the 16 distinct keys in order of first appearance (E-flat, c, C, G, D, d, B-flat, g, b-flat, f, A, e, a, E, b, f-sharp), which matches the scans; Miklós Szenthelyi's album 'The Art of the Caprice' (Apple Music, 2009; iTunes lookup id 421289372) names Nos. 4 G, 7 B-flat, 16 e, 20 b, 22 g, 23 c, 24 c; E. L. Winn, How to Study Gaviniès (Carl Fischer 1923; full text on archive.org, howtostudygavini0000edit) names the key of Nos. 4, 6-13, 17-19 and 21-24, and her numbering and tempo words match the scans. Nos. 1, 2, 3, 5, 14, 15 rest on the two scans plus the Wikipedia key list (no key is named in Winn or on the album). KEYS. The set uses only 16 keys, not 24 as retailers claim: c x4 (Nos. 2, 12, 23, 24), C x2 (3, 13), d x2 (6, 15), B-flat x2 (7, 9), g x2 (8, 22), A x2 (14, 18); no F, A-flat, D-flat, F-sharp/G-flat or B major, no c-sharp or g-sharp minor. TEMPO. Imbault and Peters differ only at No. 12 (Imbault 'Presto à mezza voce'; Peters 'Presto'), No. 15 (Imbault 'Adagio e molto sostenuto'; Peters 'Adagio molto sostenuto') and No. 24 (Imbault has no tempo word; Peters, Schirmer and Winn print 'Andante sostenuto'). Publication date: IMSLP gives none; Wikipedia says 1794, Italian Wikipedia 1800 (1794 per Fétis). LEVELS. level_guess is my estimate, relative within the book: the RCM 2021 syllabus accepts any one Matinée at Level 10 (= catalogue about 6), so nothing is rated below 6. The ranking comes from Winn's 1923 comments (easy keys and 'no serious difficulties' for 4, 5, 7, 9, 13, 14, 17; the heaviest bow and left-hand tests at 11, 15, 19 and 21-24), a violinist.com thread of 2004 (a teacher suggests Nos. 8, 12, 17 as starters; No. 1 is called hard because of its double stops) and my own reading of the scores. Treat as medium confidence. well_known is true only for Nos. 1, 4, 15, 16, where a per-number source exists (the violinist.com thread; an exam-repertoire analysis guide sold for No. 4; the Szenthelyi recording; IMSLP lists a separate arrangement of No. 15). I found no per-number syllabus lists, so the flags are anecdotal. NOT VERIFIED. AMEB (ameb.edu.au and utas.edu.au refused automated access; the only AMEB-flavoured per-number hint is a 'Level V' analysis guide for Matinée No. 4 on musicanalysis.com.au, dated 2012), ASTA CAP (handbook is members-only). University audition pages found by search (Carnegie Mellon, Colorado State, Iowa, Lynn, UMKC) name Gaviniès as an etude option but give no numbers (search summaries only; pages not opened). Other editions exist (Galamian / International Music Co. 2074, Lichtenberg / Schirmer 1908, Kross and Singer / Carl Fischer, Kalmus / Alfred); they are editions of the same book, not separate works. A 2024 Hacettepe University thesis (Z. İ. Erden, 'Pierre Gavinies'in 24 Etüdünün Keman Tekniğine Katkıları', https://openaccess.hacettepe.edu.tr/handle/11655/34876; 50 MB PDF, not opened) may contain per-study technical analysis.
